newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up at two-month high against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up at two-month high against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a two-month high of 8.2945 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2952 due to active buying by foreign banks, traders said.
It was the highest closing level since February 24 when the yuan also ended at 8.2945.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2949.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2945 and hit a high of 8.2943 early in the session. It then consolidated in a narrow range between the opening price and the intraday low of 8.2949 for the rest of the session, traders said.
Trading was less active than Tuesday with most business done at about 8.2948, traders said.
Dealers said designated foreign banks bought the yuan heavily on the market on Wednesday, helping the currency to stand firm above the psychologically important 8.2950 level.
"We believe the buying is related to the fact that foreign banks are now doing local Chinese yuan business," one dealer said. "It helped strengthen pro-yuan sentiment on the market."
China's central bank has granted approval to nine foreign banks to do local currency business. At least three have already begun limited loans and deposits.
